sourceCopy.name: RREF Calculator
sourceCopy.title: RREF Calculator Free | UsefulVerse
sourceCopy.description: Reduce a matrix to reduced row echelon form. See rank, pivot columns and row-operation steps with this free online RREF calculator.
sourceCopy.intro: Enter a rectangular matrix to calculate its reduced row echelon form (RREF), rank, pivot columns and elementary row-operation steps.
sourceCopy.howQuestion: How do you find reduced row echelon form?
sourceCopy.howAnswer: Use Gaussian elimination to create a leading 1 in each pivot column and eliminate every other value in that column. This calculator uses bounded numerical arithmetic and displays each row swap, scaling and elimination step.
sourceCopy.privacyAnswer: No. The matrix is processed in this browser and is not uploaded or saved by this tool.

fields.matrixHint: Enter one row per line. Separate columns with spaces, tabs or semicolons. Use finite decimal values; fractions such as 1/2 are not accepted.
fields.toleranceHint: Values at or below this absolute size are treated as zero. Tight tolerances may amplify rounding error.
fields.accuracyNote: Numerical result, not exact symbolic arithmetic. Up to 12 rows and columns; entries must be finite and no larger than 10⁹ in absolute value. Check the tolerance for ill-conditioned matrices.
fields.noOperations: The matrix is already in reduced row echelon form.
fields.stepsLimited: Only the first 256 row-operation steps are shown.

messages.checkInputs: Check the matrix shape, entries and tolerance.
messages.copyUnavailable: Copy is not available in this browser.

additionalFaqs.question: What does RREF mean?
additionalFaqs.answer: Reduced row echelon form has a leading 1 in each nonzero row, each pivot is the only nonzero value in its column, and pivot positions move to the right in lower rows.

additionalFaqs.question: How do I read pivot columns and rank?
additionalFaqs.answer: The listed pivot columns contain leading 1s. The rank is the number of pivot columns, or equivalently the number of nonzero rows in the RREF.

additionalFaqs.question: Is the result exact?
additionalFaqs.answer: No. This tool uses floating-point arithmetic and a selected zero tolerance. For exact rational work or ill-conditioned matrices, verify the result with an appropriate symbolic tool.
